BetRivers and Gateway Casinos Link Up in Alberta's New iGaming Market

Published August 30, 2026 · 4 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

BetRivers, the online casino and sportsbook brand operated by Rush Street Interactive, has struck a partnership with Gateway Casinos & Entertainment to link its online platform with two of Gateway's Edmonton properties: Grand Villa Casino in the ICE District and Starlight Casino at West Edmonton Mall. The deal, announced this week, connects BetRivers' digital product with joint events, cross-promotions, and brand-ambassador appearances at both physical locations.

A young market getting its first cross-channel tie-ins

The partnership lands about six weeks after Alberta opened its regulated iGaming market to licensed private operators on July 13, when 22 platforms went live on day one, including BetRivers, FanDuel, Caesars, and DraftKings. Alberta had previously run online gambling exclusively through a government-operated platform, so the July launch marked the province's first real entry of competitive private-sector iGaming — and deals like this one are an early sign of operators trying to differentiate themselves by bridging their online products with existing physical casino footprints rather than competing purely on app features or promotions.

The current agreement covers online-to-retail casino promotions only; it does not extend to BetRivers retail sportsbook operations at either Gateway property, since Alberta requires a separate license from the Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Commission for retail sports wagering, and retail books must be housed inside an approved casino, racing entertainment center, or professional sports venue.

What the companies said

Rush Street Interactive CEO Richard Schwartz framed the deal around giving customers "more ways to play, more reasons to visit, and more to look forward to," while Gateway CEO Tolek Strukoff said the goal is for Albertans to have three strong places to play, whether online or in person. Neither company disclosed financial terms.

Why it matters

Alberta's iGaming market is still in its early innings, and how quickly it grows is being watched closely across the industry — analyst estimates cited around the market's launch projected roughly CA$390 million in operator revenue and about CA$76 million in provincial tax in the market's first stretch, with some longer-range projections running considerably higher over a couple of years. Partnerships that connect an operator's app to a well-known physical venue are a common early-market playbook, aimed at converting existing casino visitors into online customers and vice versa. For US bettors and players, the Alberta rollout is also a useful preview of how a newly opened, competitive iGaming market tends to develop in its first months — rapid operator launches followed by a wave of retail-digital integration deals like this one.
